//note: The PostgreSQL role this identity connects as must hold BYPASSRLS or be a superuser. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY applies to the table owner, so the application role cannot pg_dump its own rows -- it produces a structurally valid dump with none of its data. tests/integration/test_restore_drill.py asserts this directly.

Statement.//: Read-only on the evidence bucket. A backup that could write to the bucket it is copying could corrupt the thing it exists to preserve.
A different bucket, in a different account where the account structure allows it. A backup in the same blast radius as the thing it protects is not a backup.

Explicit Deny. The identity that writes backups must not be able to remove them: ransomware's first move is to delete the backups with the credentials it already has. Expiry is a bucket lifecycle rule managed by a different identity.
Encrypt only. This identity seals archives; opening one is a restore, performed by a person during an incident under a different role. See scripts/restore.py.
